To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rate of violence by patients with mental disorders was not different from that of others in their communities, but the rate of violence was higher among those patients with co occurring substance abuse.

the rate of violence by patients with mental disorders was not significantly higher than the rate of violence of others living in the neighborhoods where patients resided after discharge from acute psychiatric facilities; the rate of violence was significantly higher among those with symptoms of substance abuse than among those without symptoms of substance use disorders; and the rate of substance abuse was significantly higher among patients than among the comparison sample.

the prevalence of community assault by people discharged from psychiatric facilities was not significantly higher than the prevalence of community assaults by people without mental disorders in the same neighborhoods, and the prevalence of community sexual assaults by people discharged from these facilities was significantly higher than the community sexual assault prevalence in the same neighborhoods.
